description.p: Plug in your Kobo e-reader and Kollate brings in everything you marked while reading: highlights, notes, handwritten markups, notebooks and the words you looked up. It never changes anything on the Kobo, and never goes online.

ul.li: Reads your handwriting as text, with a small model that runs on your computer; what you underlined comes word for word from the book
Curate as you read: a star, a question mark or a #tag in the margin files the passage, and a circled word goes to your vocabulary
Imports Basic and Advanced notebooks, every page redrawn and read
Finds the sentence each looked-up word came from, with an offline dictionary definition
Triage new highlights in an inbox from the keyboard; star, tag, edit and search everything
Share a highlight as a quote card, or email it to yourself
Sync notes to an Obsidian vault, and export Anki decks, JSON, CSV or Readwise CSV

description.p: Getting ready for Flathub.

ul.li: Reading a lot of handwriting at once, as after a first import, now shows how far along it is
A fuller description and screenshots for software centres

description.p: Quote cards: share a highlight as an image, or send it by email. And dictionaries for more languages, a click away.

ul.li: Share as Image… turns any highlight, note, markup or notebook page into a card, set in the Literata typeface, square or tall
Six palettes, including one tinted with the highlight's own Kobo colour; a markup's card can show the page with your ink
Copy the card, save it, or open an email in your email app with it attached. Set your own address in Preferences to send cards to yourself
Dictionaries for 16 more languages, as easy as handwriting models: Preferences suggests the languages your books are in, with a download link for each

description.p: Small improvements to exports, and a new project page.

ul.li: On Anki cards, the gloss you wrote beside a circled word stands apart from the dictionary's definition
Obsidian notes no longer give handwritten markups a highlight colour

description.p: Fixes for reading handwriting.

ul.li: Passages you mark on a page are listed in page order, not the order you marked them in
A word an underline runs on to past a full stop, or a stray bracket, is left out of the marked text
If reading your handwriting fails, Kollate now says why, instead of leaving your markups unread without a word

description.p: Curate while you read, with a mark in the margin, as readers have for two thousand years. Kollate reads the mark along with your handwriting and does the filing.

ul.li: A star or NB stars a passage, a question mark tags it as a question, and #word tags it; type the same marks as a highlight's note on any Kobo
Circle a word to learn it: it goes to Vocabulary with the book's sentence and a definition, and a note written beside it becomes your gloss
Small circles around a word are no longer mistaken for handwriting; your markups are read once more after updating

description.p: Kollate now imports the notebooks on a stylus Kobo, Basic and Advanced alike, and reads their handwriting on your computer. The Kobo itself only converts Advanced notebooks, and only when you ask.

ul.li: Each notebook appears as a book, and its pages in a new Notebooks view: your ink redrawn, with its writing as searchable, editable text
Drawings are left out of the text; pages you write more on or erase are read again at the next import
Qwen3-VL 2B is now the recommended handwriting model: it reads real notes as well as the 4B, and is smaller and faster

description.p: Kollate now recognises the Kobo Clara Colour by name, and is tested on it with Kobo Store books alongside sideloaded ones.
Kollate now works with black-and-white Kobos as well as colour ones: it's tested on a Kobo Clara 2E alongside the Libra Colour. Together with reading your handwriting (since 0.1.7), this makes 0.2.0.

ul.li: Books you've since moved or removed on the Kobo keep a proper title and author, instead of a file name
Context sentences for vocabulary now come from many more books: those with embedded fonts were wrongly treated as locked
Footnote numbers no longer end up in context sentences

description.p: Preferences now says which handwriting model is in use when only one is installed, instead of showing a checkbox that did nothing. Kollate also has a user guide, linked from its project page.
Handwritten notes with wide gaps between words are now read as one note, in the right order. They could be split into pieces and read out of order before.

Kollate can now read your stylus handwriting. Download one of three local models (recommended: Qwen3-VL 4B, 3.3 GB) with the links in Preferences and add it; after each import, Kollate reads your margin notes and takes the exact words you underlined or circled from the book. It all happens on your computer, never online, and every reading is a suggestion you can correct.

ul.li: Fixed: in the Flatpak, a markup's page could appear shifted under the ink
Handwritten notes appear in the Notes view and in search
Obsidian notes show a markup's ink along with its text

description.p: Handwritten markups now show your ink. The Kobo saves the page and the ink as separate files, and Kollate was only showing the page. Markups are now shown zoomed in on the handwriting and the text it marks, so notes are readable at a glance; Open Page Image still shows the whole page.

ul.li: The Obsidian export includes the ink too, replacing earlier page images

description.p: Kollate now imports from Kobo database versions it hasn't been tested with yet, instead of possibly failing without explanation. The first time it sees a new version, it tells you and offers a Report button that opens a compatibility report with your Kobo's details filled in.

ul.li: Selected highlights and the "deleted on Kobo" label keep their colours on older GNOME versions, such as Ubuntu 24.04
Releases are now built by GitHub Actions from the tagged source, with signed build provenance

description.p: In the Flatpak, the Obsidian folder is now shown as its real location (for example ~/Notes/Reading) instead of an internal sandbox path. The check that stops Kollate writing to your Kobo now also sees through those paths, so a folder on the e-reader is refused even when chosen through the file picker.

Vocabulary definitions now come from the English Wiktionary (over 800,000 words, compiled by reader.dict) instead of WordNet. Words you've looked up are re-defined automatically, and definitions you wrote yourself are kept. Dictionaries for other languages can be added in DictFile format, and Preferences links to where to get them.

ul.li: Preferences lists dictionaries by language and explains how they're used
Notifications now appear on top of the Preferences and Export windows
Clearer explanation of where to write your own notes in Obsidian

description.p: Kollate now refuses to save anything onto your Kobo, even if you choose it as an export, Obsidian or library location. The e-reader is only ever read.
Highlights deleted on the Kobo are now easier to track:

ul.li: The import summary reports highlights deleted on (and restored to) the Kobo
A Deleted on Kobo view lists them
A new preference can move them to Trash automatically

description.p: A new Books page shows your library as covers, sorted by most recent; the sidebar keeps your five latest books, and books with nothing left to show are hidden.

Search is now always visible, starring a highlight in the Inbox also keeps it, and you can select several highlights to keep, archive, star or trash them at once, or keep the whole Inbox. A new Keyboard Shortcuts window (Ctrl+?) lists every shortcut.
First release: import, curation, vocabulary enrichment and export.
